text:
Enthalpy of sublimation of iodine is 24 cal $g^{–1}$ at $200 ^{o}C$. If specific heat of $I_{2}(s)$ and $l_{2} ($vap) are 0.055 and
0.031 cal $g^{–1}K$
$^{–1}$
respectively, then enthalpy of sublimation of iodine at $250 ^{o}C$ in cal $g^{–1}$
 is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Kirchoff's Equation :

$\frac{\Delta H_{T2}-\Delta H_{T1}}{T_{2}-T_{1}}=\Delta (C_{p})$

Sublimation of iodine :

$I_{2}(s)$ $\to$ $I_{2}(g)$

$\frac{\Delta H_{250\circ C}-\Delta H_{200\circ C}}{250-200}=C_{p}[I_{2}(g)]-C_{p}[I_{2}(s)]$

$\frac{\Delta H_{250\circ C}-24}{50}=(0.031-0.055)$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta H_{250^{\circ }C}$ = 22.8 cal $g^{–1}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot

text:
An ideal gas is allowed to expand from 1 L to 10 L against a constant external pressure of 1 bar. The work
done in kJ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
This is an irreversible process as gas is expanding against a constant external pressure.

Work done in irreversible process

$W = - P_{$ext}$\Delta$V

= - 1 bar $\times$  9 L

$= - 10^{5} Pa$ $\times$ 9 $\times$ $10^{-3} m^{3}$

= - 9 $\times$ $10^{2} N-m$

= - 900 J

= - 0.9 kJ

text:
In the following reaction; xA $\to$ yB

$\log _{10}\left [-\frac{d[A]}{dt}\right ]=\log _{10}\left [\frac{d[B]}{dt}\right ]+0.3010$

'A' and 'B' respectively can be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
xA $\to$ yB

$\frac{1}{x}\left \{-\frac{d[A]}{dt}\right \}=\frac{1}{y}\left \{\frac{d[B]}{dt}\right \}$

$\Rightarrow$ $-\frac{d[A]}{dt}=\frac{x}{y}\left \{\frac{d[B]}{dt}\right \}$

Taking log both sides, we get

$\Rightarrow$ $\log _{10}\left [-\frac{d[A]}{dt}\right ]=\log _{10}\left [\frac{d[B]}{dt}\right ]+\log _{10}\left (\frac{x}{y}\right )$

Given that,

$\log _{10}\left [-\frac{d[A]}{dt}\right ]=\log _{10}\left [\frac{d[B]}{dt}\right ]+0.3010$

So, by comparing both of them we get

$\log _{10}\left (\frac{x}{y}\right )$ = 0.3010 = $\log _{10}(2)$

$\therefore$ $\frac{x}{y}$ = 2

$\Rightarrow$ x = 2y

If x = 2 then y = 1

The reaction is of type 2A $\to$ B

So possible reaction is

$2C_{2}H_{4}$ $\to$ $C_{4}H_{8}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot

text:
The complex ion that will lose its crystal field stabilization energy upon oxidation of its metal to +3 state is :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
1,10-Phenanthroline is a strong-field ligand, so the octahedral complexes are low-spin; with pairing energy ignored, $\text{CFSE}=(-0.4n_{t_{2g}}+0.6n_{e_{g}})\Delta _{o}$.

Fe: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$ ($d^{6}$, $t_{2g}^{6}$) has $-2.4\Delta _{o}$, and $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ ($d^{5}$, $t_{2g}^{5}$) has $-2.0\Delta _{o}$, so CFSE is lost on oxidation.

Co: $\mathrm{Co}{}^{2+}$ ($d^{7}$, $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{1}$) has $-1.8\Delta _{o}$, and $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ ($d^{6}$, $t_{2g}^{6}$) has $-2.4\Delta _{o}$, so CFSE is gained.

Ni: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ ($d^{8}$, $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{2}$) has $-1.2\Delta _{o}$, and $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{3+}$ ($d^{7}$, $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{1}$) has $-1.8\Delta _{o}$, so CFSE is gained.

Zn: $\mathrm{Zn}{}^{2+}$ ($d^{10}$) has zero CFSE and is not oxidised to +3.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot

text:
Complete removal of both the axial ligands (along the z-axis) from an octahedral complex leads to which of
the following splitting patterns? (relative orbital energies not on scale).
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Removing both ligands on the $z$-axis turns the octahedral field into a square planar field, with the four remaining ligands on the $\pm x$ and $\pm y$ axes.

The $d_{x^{2}-y^{2}}$ orbital points its lobes directly at the four ligands, so it stays highest in energy.

The $d_{xy}$ orbital lies in the ligand plane but between the axes, so it comes next.

The $d_{z^{2}}$ orbital loses its strong repulsion from the axial ligands and drops sharply; only its small ring in the $xy$ plane still faces the ligands, so it lies below $d_{xy}$.

The $d_{xz}$ and $d_{yz}$ orbitals both have a $z$ component and only weak contact with the in-plane ligands, so they are lowest and remain degenerate.

$d_{x^{2}-y^{2}}>d_{xy}>d_{z^{2}}>d_{xz}=d_{yz}$

Figure (C) places $d_{z^{2}}$ above $d_{xy}$, which ignores the loss of both axial ligands.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot

text:
5 moles of $AB_{2}$ weigh $125 × 10^{–3}$
 kg and 10 moles of $A_{2}B_{2}$ weigh $300 × 10^{–3}$
 kg. The molar mass of $A (M_{A})$
and molar mass of $B (M_{B})$ in kg mol$^{–1}$ are:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Molar weight of $'A' = M_{A}$

Molar weight of $'B' = M_{B}$

Molar mass of $AB_{2} = M_{A} + 2M_{B}$

Molar mass of $A_{2}B_{2} = 2(M_{A} + M_{B})$

5 mol $AB_{2}$ weighs 125 g

$\therefore$ $AB_{2} = 25 g/$mol

10 mol $A_{2}B_{2}$ weighs 300 g

$\therefore$ $A_{2}B_{2} = 30 g/$mol

So, $M_{A} + 2M_{B} = 25 ..............(1)$

and $2(M_{A} + M_{B}) = 30 ..............(2)$

By solving (1) and (2),

$M_{A} = 5 gm = 5$ $\times$ $10^{-3} kg$

$M_{B} = 10 gm = 10$ $\times$ $10^{-3} kg$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot

text: The correct statement among the following is :
options: (SiH$_{3})_{3}N$ is planar and more basic than $(CH_{3})_{3}N$
(SiH$_{3})_{3}N$ is pyramidal and more basic than $(CH_{3})_{3}N$
(SiH$_{3})_{3}N$ is pyramidal and less basic than $(CH_{3})_{3}N$
(SiH$_{3})_{3}N$ is planar and less basic than $(CH_{3})_{3}N$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]



[IMG]


In $(CH_{3})_{3}N$, one lone pair and 3 sigma bond present. So its shape is pyramidal.

But in (SiH$_{3})_{3}N$, due to backbonding lone pair of N shift to vacant 3d orbital of Si. So now N have only 3 sigma bond and hybridization is $sp^{2}$, that is why it has triangular planar geometry.

As in (SiH$_{3})_{3}N$. nitrogen(N) don't have any lone pair to donate but in $(CH_{3})_{3}N$, lone pair of nitrogen(N) can easily be donated. That is why $(CH_{3})_{3}N$ is more basic.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th April Morning Slot
